model: Gibson Les Paul Standard, 1958-60 ("59 Burst") - carved maple cap on mahogany, set neck, 2 PAF humbuckers, ABR-1 + stopbar

PRIMARY SOURCE. 1:1 raster blueprint (300 dpi, 1 cm grid) "1950s LP Front Perspective": used to cross-check body 43.85 x 33.40, nut position, fret positions, toggle/strap-button location, binding 0.178 x 0.596, poker-chip size
1959 LP neck profile templates at 1st/11th fret (neck-only depth 1.69 / 1.88 cm, width 4.44 / 5.27 cm)

measured real '59: mahogany 1.75-1.785 in, rim (back to top of binding) 1.93-2.02 in, max 2.34 in between bridge and bridge pickup
'Beauty of the Burst' data, 1959 average neck depth 0.879 in (1st fret) / 0.970 in (11th) / 0.979 in (12th, calc); 1958 0.900/0.989, 1960 0.831/0.912

neck.profile: C (1959 medium rounded C; 1958 is fatter, 1960 slim)
neck.heel: Long-tenon set neck. Tenon 3.82 wide (x -1.91..+1.91), runs from the body edge (y 43.79) into the neck pickup cavity and ends with a rounded tongue at y 33.07 (tenon route ends y 32.94). Tenon is ~4.25 deep below the neck plane up to the fretboard end, the last ~2.9 cm (under the neck pickup) is a 2.0 thick tongue at the bottom of the mortise. Mortise floor follows the 4 deg neck plane. Outside the body the heel flares from normal neck depth starting ~2.7 cm before the body edge (y ~46.5) down to within ~0.6 cm of the body back plane at the body edge (short concave heel curve, radius ~2 cm, rounded half-oval heel cap). Neck width where it meets the body 5.45; the cutaway inner wall on the treble side is flush with the neck side (x +2.71).
neck.actualFretScaleNote: Gibson cut 1950s fret slots for ~24.56-24.62 in (62.39-62.53 cm) although the nominal scale is 24.75 in; use scaleLength (nominal) for nut/bridge placement.

carve.profileNotes: Arched maple cap over a flat mahogany back. Rim (back to top of binding ledge) 5.00 cm (real 1.93-2.02 in; template 5.19). Mahogany back 4.45 (1.75 in) + maple cap ~0.55 at the edge. Crown 0.93 above rim => 5.93 total (real max 2.34 in = 5.94). Along the centerline: flat ledge from the tail to y 2.30, steady rise to a broad plateau y 19.7-23.1 (max at y 21.1, i.e. between the ABR-1 and the bridge pickup), then a slow fall toward the neck: h 0.83 at y 28.5, 0.57 at y 35, reaching the rim level at the neck joint (y 43.4-43.8). Cross sections (see crossSections, heights above rim, x in body coords) are symmetric about x=0 with crown on the centerline: 0.59 (upper bout y 35.1), 0.85 (waist y 28.5), 0.98 (lower bout y 21.1), 0.90 (widest y 14.7). Interpolate between crossSections and centerlineProfile; carveStartOutline (h=0) bounds the carved area.
carve.recurveNotes: No dish below rim level: the recurve is a concave S-transition from a FLAT binding ledge into the convex crown. Flat ledge width measured inward from the edge: ~2.9 (upper bout), ~1.1-1.8 (waist), ~3.6 (lower bout behind bridge pickup), ~4.1 (widest lower bout), ~2.3 at the tail on the centerline; ~0 where the carve meets the neck joint. Inside the ledge the surface rises concave (the recurve) to the steepest point = inflection (recurveToConvexInflectionX per section, ~2.0-2.3 cm inside the ledge end), then convex to the crown. The ledge line itself = carveStartOutline.

crossSections.where: upper bout, level with top edge of neck pickup ring
lower bout, just behind bridge pickup ring (in front of ABR-1)
widest part of lower bout, just behind stopbar studs

bridge.type: Gibson ABR-1 tune-o-matic (thumbwheels on posts) + stop bar tailpiece on two studs

details.abr1Note: bass post 0.39 further from the neck than treble post; nominal 24.75 in line passes through the post midpoint

pickups.note: bridge ring is the taller of the two rings (follows the carve slope); footprint identical

controls.knobNote: pot shaft centres; gold top-hat knobs. Volumes are the pair nearer the bridge; neck controls are the inner (string-side) column.

jack.note: side jack on lower treble bout rim with cream rectangular jack plate

pickguard.note: raised cream pickguard (does not touch the top). Inner edge steps around the two pickup rings; mounted with a screw/spacer at the neck end and a bracket under the bridge pickup ring.

headstock.notes: Outline bottom edge (y 0.28, width 4.26) is the headstock-side face of the 0.28 cm nut; scale zero is y 0. Width 7.78 at the top corners; top corners y 16.69, centre notch y 17.20, open-book ears y 17.51. 17 deg back angle starts at the nut (Gibson used 17 deg until ~1965, 14 deg after). Kluson 3-a-side, bell truss rod cover (wide end toward the nut).

notes: Coordinates: body y=0 at tail on centerline, +y to neck, bass side -x. Body 43.80 x 33.06 (published 17.25 x 13 in = 43.82 x 33.02). nutY = saddleLineY + scaleLength = 81.61; independent neck-length measurements put the nut at 81.59 (+-0.08). Neck is set at 4 deg: the neck glue plane (fretboard underside) is at rim height at the body edge (y 43.79), drops below the rim toward the nut and rises into the body, reaching 0.56 above rim at the fretboard end, where the 0.55-0.6 fretboard top is 1.13 above rim (the fretboard extension rests on the carved top). Plan-view y values here are unrolled (cos 4 deg foreshortening of the neck, 0.1 cm, ignored). Fretboard (bound, 22 frets, 12 in radius) extends past the 22nd fret to y 35.70 and stops just short of the neck pickup ring. Top binding is flush with the flat ledge; carve starts at carveStartOutline. Toggle is on the upper bass bout, controls and side jack on the lower treble bout, upper strap button on the bass-side rim next to the neck heel. Pickguard is raised ~0.6-1.0 above the top. Knob positions are pot shafts from the template; knob skirts ~1.9 dia.
